starter.index.html: Falling Skies
starter.README.md:
# Falling Skies

Open index.html without a server. Edit script.js and reload the page.

The blue 30-by-60 player starts at (260,400) on a 550-by-500 canvas. Left and right move eight pixels per simulation tick and clamp the entire rectangle inside the canvas. After a three-second countdown, radius-15 circles fall eight pixels per tick, with a new circle every ten ticks. The score increases once per two seconds of survival. The simulation uses 60 ticks per second, independent of display refresh rate.

Complete circleTouchesRectangle and stepGame in script.js. Clamp the circle center to the rectangle's nearest point. Compare squared distance to radius squared; equality is contact. Check every circle before declaring the player safe. Remove all circles beyond the bottom without skipping adjacent entries. A hit changes the state to lost once and freezes play. Restart creates a fresh countdown. Hold the arrow keys or the on-screen direction controls; releasing focus clears held input.

Trace a harmless first circle followed by a circle at the player's center: the second circle must end play. A circle centered at (245,400) exactly touches the player's left top corner; (246,386) is outside its radius despite overlapping bounding boxes. Review CASES.md, then compare the complete reference only after attempting both functions.

The starter keeps the supplied renderer and input wiring; complete its two TODO functions.
starter.CASES.md:
# Falling Skies cases

1. First obstacle harmless, second centered on the player: lost.
2. Tangent circle at (245,400),radius15: contact. Corner near-miss at (246,386): no contact.
3. Hold either direction for 100 ticks: x stays in [0,520].
4. Countdown 180 ticks: no falling objects before it ends. Survive 120 further ticks: score1.
5. Put two consecutive circles below y515: both removed.
6. After lost, 300 updates preserve all state; Restart resets score and countdown.

starter.index.html: 2D Breakout
starter.README.md:
# 2D Breakout

Open index.html without a server. Edit script.js and reload the page.

The 480-by-320 canvas contains fifteen bricks, a radius-10 ball, a 75-by-10 paddle and three lives. The ball starts at (240,290), moving (2,-2) per simulation tick. A new life resets its motion to (3,-3), preserving the original reference's rule. Arrow keys move the paddle seven pixels per tick; pointer movement maps the displayed canvas position into its logical coordinates. The paddle remains wholly inside the canvas.

Complete circleTouchesRectangle and stepGame in script.js. Compare the ball's radius with a brick's nearest point, mark a hit brick inactive, increase score once and reverse the collision axis. A downward crossing of the paddle top reflects the ball upward. Crossing completely below the canvas costs exactly one life. Reset the ball when lives remain; otherwise enter lost. Removing the fifteenth brick enters won. Both terminal states freeze the model until Restart, with a message on the canvas and in the status line.

Use the CASES.md boundary checks: a ball can touch a brick before its center enters it; a miss costs one life, not one per later frame. Compare the saved reference after completing the starter. Hold a direction control or use the pointer to play; observe all three lives and restart without browser alerts.

The starter keeps the supplied renderer and input wiring; complete its two TODO functions.
starter.CASES.md:
# 2D Breakout cases

1. Brick x30,y30,width75,height20; ball center (20,40),radius10: contact.
2. Ball (19,19),radius10: corner near-miss.
3. Paddle pointer and keys clamp x in [0,405] at both display sizes.
4. Three separate misses use three lives; later updates preserve lives0 and lost.
5. Final live brick hit: score15,won; later updates preserve state.
6. Restart resets all fifteen bricks,three lives and score0.

starter.index.html: Asteroids
starter.README.md:
# Asteroids

Open index.html without a server. Edit script.js and reload the page.

The 550-by-500 canvas begins with the original triangular ship at (100,100). A and D rotate five degrees per simulation tick; W moves one pixel in the ship's forward direction. The on-screen controls provide the same actions. Space and F share one ten-tick firing cooldown. Bullets move five pixels per tick; radius-50 asteroids enter from a random edge every five seconds and move two pixels per tick. Motion uses 60 simulation ticks per second. The ship and asteroids wrap at the canvas boundary.

Complete shipTouchesCircle and stepGame in script.js. Rotate the three local triangle vertices around the ship center. A circle hits if its center lies inside the triangle or its distance from any edge is at most its radius. Bullet collision uses squared center distance and the combined radii. Remove the hit parent, add two half-radius children only when their radius exceeds ten, and score once. Keep bullets in the single game loop, removing spent or off-screen entries.

Death freezes firing, spawning and score until Restart. Focus loss releases all controls. Check CASES.md for the ten-tick cooldown, a single split and a stopped terminal state. Increasing bullet speed requires a swept collision method; this assignment's fixed speeds are the stated model. Compare the complete reference after attempting both functions.

The starter keeps the supplied renderer and input wiring; complete its two TODO functions.
starter.CASES.md:
# Asteroids cases

1. Hold Space or F for ten ticks: one shot; tick11 permits the next. Switching keys cannot bypass cooldown.
2. Bullet touches a radius50 asteroid: score+1,two radius25 children,spent bullet removed.
3. Hit radius12.5: score+1,no children.
4. A circle touching a triangle edge or vertex hits; a bounding-box-only corner overlap does not.
5. Death freezes bullet,asteroid and score state even while Fire remains held.
6. Resize preserves logical550-by500 geometry; Restart resets ship,score,bullets and spawn timer.

starter.index.html: Animated Starfield
starter.README.md:
# Animated Starfield

Open index.html without a server. Edit script.js and reload the page.

Create a black field of one hundred white stars. Each object stores x, y, size and downward velocity. Sizes range from one to four pixels; velocities range from fifteen to thirty pixels per second. The original CodePen uses Babel, but this implementation uses ordinary browser JavaScript and needs no compiler or external scripts. Open index.html without a server.

Complete stepGame and resizeStars in script.js. At thirty simulation ticks per second, a star moves velocity divided by thirty pixels per tick. When its y coordinate exceeds the field height, replace that entry with a new star at y=0. Preserve the array length. On resize, scale existing positions by new width/old width and new height/old height before storing the new dimensions. A single animation loop draws the black background and then the white squares.

In CASES.md, trace a star with velocity=30 from y=10 to y=11 after one tick. A star that moves past the bottom returns to the top without increasing density. Resize the window and confirm that all stars remain within the new field. Restart creates a fresh field without adding another loop. The assignment follows Juni Learning's visible Starfield task; its original reference credits the CodeProject article recorded in SOURCES.md.

The starter keeps the supplied renderer and input wiring; complete its two TODO functions.
starter.CASES.md:
# Animated Starfield cases

1. Velocity30,y10: after one tick,y11.
2. A star crossing below height respawns at y0 with a valid x,size and velocity.
3. All updates preserve exactly100 stars.
4. Resize from550x500 to275x250 halves every position and retains100 entries.
5. White star squares remain visible on black at mobile and desktop widths.
6. Restart keeps one animation loop and one hundred stars.
